newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian coalition plays down Rao's legal problems.
newsitem.headline: Indian coalition plays down Rao's legal problems.

text.p: India's ruling centre-left coalition shrugged off turmoil within its Congress party ally on Friday and said legal troubles plaguing former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao did not threaten the government.
Rao was charged on Thursday in a forgery case and was denied legal protection against arrest in a separate criminal conspiracy case.
Rao's woes emboldened the rightist Hindu opposition, which predicted growing strains between the 13-party United Front coalition and Congress.
"Our confidence has gone up," said L.K. Advani, president of the rightist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The United Front and Congress joined hands to topple a 12-day-old BJP government following general elections that returned the BJP as the largest group in parliament

Senior BJP leader Jaswant Singh, who was finance minister in the short-lived BJP government, said the charges against Rao spelled trouble for the United Front, especially in local polls in populous Uttar Pradesh starting next week.
But United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said there was no threat to the coalition.

"There is no reason why these cases should have any impact on the longevity or durability or stability of the Deve Gowda government," Reddy told a news conference. "There is absolutely no room to think that the Congress party will review its position on the issue at all."
Deve Gowda's minority coalition lacks an outright majority in the 545-seat lower house of parliament and depends on the support of Congress's 140 deputies.
Congress finished second in general elections ended in May behind the BJP, which stepped down when it failed to muster enough support to win a confidence vote.
Rao's lawyer said on Thursday that he expected the former Congress party president to be arrested on Monday, when Rao has been ordered to appear in a Delhi court in the conspiracy case.
A court on Thursday rejected Rao's plea for anticipatory bail, which would have protected him against arrest. Legal experts said he could request ordinary bail if arrested.
Two others accused in the conspiracy to cheat case are currently under judicial custody in Bangkok's Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison with some 10,000 inmates, awaiting trial.

Newspapers said authorities were preparing for the possibility that the former prime minister might be arrested in the cheating case and put under police custody ahead of the trial. Rao has denied any involvement in the 13-year-old case.

The Asian Age newspaper said authorities were preparing a bungalow in central Delhi as a "special prison" for Rao. One official said there was a possibility that Rao, if arrested, would be confined to his home.

Share prices on the Bombay Stock Exchange fell on the news that Rao had been charged in the forgery case and denied anticipatory bail. The exchange's benchmark index was down 50.09 points, or 1.51 percent, at 3,256.96 at 15:29 p.m. (0959 GMT).
Brokers said Rao's political worries and their potential effect on the coalition government had created uncertainty that undermined share prices.
